doc.title: Paquito D'Rivera — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Repertoire and purpose of the officially formed big band
summary: The orchestra played music banned months earlier, such as Route 66 and Mancini, on imported instruments; Paquito believes it was formed to counter the image that the revolution blocked jazz, and it got him out of the army.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: So this group that you became a part of, Orchestra Cubana de Musica Moderna, what was the repertoire of that orchestra?
Music that was forbidden six months before. For example, “Route 66.”
You were in the army, and then you finished the army after six months, right?
Yea because they formed this orchestra, the Orchestra Cubana Musica Moderna.
This orchestra was your exit from the army?
How did that happen; how did this orchestra come together?
I am almost sure that this orchestra was formed in order to improve or to deny the impression that the revolution was blocking Jazz music.
So this was an officially sanctioned orchestra?
Sanctioned meaning that the government saw this orchestra as a vehicle. The government tolerated this orchestra to a certain extent—

Nobody knows; suddenly, six months before that, we, I wanted to play that type of music. We play in the jam sessions very quietly, you know. In order to avoid that type of music, conflict with the government for playing and all that, we started to avoid conflict with the government for playing foreign music. So suddenly they decided to form this orchestra for playing foreign music. As simple as that, foreign music; most of the music—except for this one time I had a very Americanized arrangement of “Cuando Novela”—the rest of the repertoire was music by Peter Gun, Heavy Mancini, for instrument. And the instruments were imported from France and some from the United States and Canada; they sent saxophones, guitars, and all that, in order to play American music.
